title: Simplicial-presheaf Bousfield models identify local infinity categories
statement:
Use the universe and infinity-category conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Let $D$ be a small ordinary category and put $\mathsf U(D)=\operatorname{Fun}(D^{\mathrm{op}},\mathsf{sSet})$, where simplicial sets are as in [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], with the Kan model structure (monomorphisms, weak homotopy equivalences and Kan fibrations). Give $\mathsf U(D)$ its projective model structure, whose weak equivalences and fibrations are objectwise. For a small set $S$ of arrows of $\mathsf U(D)$, let $L_S\mathsf U(D)$ be its left Bousfield localization: cofibrations are unchanged and weak equivalences $W_S$ are maps inducing equivalences of derived mapping spaces into every projectively fibrant $S$-local presheaf. An object $Z$ is $S$-local when $\operatorname{Map}^{h}(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^{h}(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for all $(A\to B)\in S$; derived mapping spaces use projective cofibrant and fibrant replacements. Let $\mathcal S$ be the infinity category of small spaces and set $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(N(D)^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$. Objectwise passage from simplicial sets to spaces identifies
$$N(\mathsf U(D))[W_{\mathrm{obj}}^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\mathcal P,$$
where $W_{\mathrm{obj}}$ denotes objectwise weak homotopy equivalences. Write $\overline S$ for the small set of arrows of $\mathcal P$ obtained from $S$ under this equivalence, and let $\mathcal P_{\overline S\text{-loc}}$ be the full subcategory of $Z$ such that $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(A,Z)$ is an equivalence for every $(A\to B)\in\overline S$. There is an equivalence
$$N(L_S\mathsf U(D))[W_S^{-1}]_\infty\simeq\mathcal P_{\overline S\text{-loc}}.$$
All localizations here are universal homotopy coherent localizations: restriction on functor infinity categories into any infinity category identifies the target with the full subcategory of functors inverting the indicated arrows. In particular the comparisons retain mapping spaces and coherent compositions.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.4.4, Proposition A.3.7.3 and Remark A.3.7.5, and the localized-presheaf part of the proof of Proposition A.3.7.6 (printed pp. 258, 908-912). Combined with HA Theorem 1.3.4.20 to express the simplicial nerve as homotopy coherent localization. Read online, not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal M=\mathsf U(D)$. By [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model], the projective model structure is left proper, combinatorial and simplicial with functorial factorizations, and its fibrant objects are the objectwise Kan presheaves. This also supplies the combinatorial simplicial Kan model structure on $\mathsf{sSet}$. These are the hypotheses needed below; projective cofibrancy is not being identified with objectwise cofibrancy.

source.place: Proposition A.3.3.2 and Remarks A.3.3.4-A.3.3.5; Example A.3.2.18.

proof.text: Regard $D^{\mathrm{op}}$ as a simplicial category with discrete mapping simplicial sets. Such sets are Kan, and $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(D^{\mathrm{op}})=N(D^{\mathrm{op}})=N(D)^{\mathrm{op}}$: a functor from the thickening of $[n]$ to a category with discrete mapping spaces is just a composable string, all its higher compatibility maps being forced by composition. By the counit clause of [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification], $u:\mathfrak C[N(D^{\mathrm{op}})]\to D^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Apply its diagram comparison with $K=N(D^{\mathrm{op}})$ and target $\mathsf{sSet}$, using the projective structure supplied by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. By [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], the two bifibrant nerves represent $N(\mathcal M)[W_{\mathrm{obj}}^{-1}]_\infty$ and $\mathcal S$, respectively. Composing the comparisons gives $E:\mathcal M_\infty\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(N(D)^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)=\mathcal P$. Since the diagram comparison is induced by evaluation, its value at $d$ is passage from the simplicial set $F(d)$ to its space; this specifies the claimed objectwise comparison, on arrows and coherent diagrams as well as on objects.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.4.4 and Remark 4.2.4.5; Theorem 2.2.5.1. HA Theorem 1.3.4.20 identifies the bifibrant nerves with universal localizations.

proof.text: To apply the model-localization existence theorem to arbitrary $S$, choose one functorial projective cofibrant replacement $Q$ with natural trivial fibration $q:Q\to\operatorname{id}$. For each $f:A\to B$ in $S$, factor $Qf:QA\to QB$ as $QA\xrightarrow{i_f}B_f\xrightarrow{p_f}QB$, with $i_f$ a cofibration and $p_f$ a trivial fibration. Thus both endpoints of $i_f$ are cofibrant. The squares $i_f\to Qf\to f$, with vertical maps $(1,p_f)$ and $(q_A,q_B)$, have objectwise weak-equivalence verticals. The mapping-space comparison of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] therefore identifies their derived mapping-space tests against any fibrant $Z$. Put $T=\{i_f:f\in S\}$. It is small, has the same fibrant local objects as $S$, and hence has exactly the same local-equivalence class $W_S$. This uses two-out-of-three for equivalences of spaces, and does not assume that $f$ or its endpoints are cofibrant.

source.place: Proposition A.3.7.3 and Remark A.3.7.5; explicit replacement of arbitrary arrows by cofibrations between cofibrant objects.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-simplicial-bousfield-model-structure] to $\mathcal M$ and the small set $T$ from step 3. Its hypotheses of left properness, combinatoriality and simpliciality hold by step 1, and $T$ consists of cofibrations between cofibrant objects. The resulting model has unchanged cofibrations and weak equivalences $W_S$ by step 3, so it is exactly the model denoted $L_S\mathsf U(D)$ in the statement. Its fibrant objects are precisely the projectively fibrant $S$-local presheaves. Its simplicial enrichment is the original one, and it has functorial factorizations. Denote its coherent localization by $\mathcal L$.

The identity adjunction of [lem-coef-simplicial-bousfield-model-structure] induces an infinity adjunction $L:\mathcal M_\infty\rightleftarrows\mathcal L:J$ by [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction]. Let $\mathcal A=(L_S\mathcal M)^{cf}$ and $\mathcal B=\mathcal M^{cf}$. Unchanged cofibrations and the original fibrancy of localized fibrant objects give a full simplicial inclusion $I:\mathcal A\hookrightarrow\mathcal B$. It is the identity on each enriched mapping simplicial set because the localization retains the enrichment. The nerve-localization comparisons of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] identify $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(I)$ with $J$: on the ordinary category of localized bifibrant objects both are the original localization of its inclusion into $\mathcal M$, since the right-derived identity needs no fibrant replacement there. That ordinary bifibrant category localizes equivalently onto $\mathcal L$ by the same cited theorem, so this agreement determines the functors on $\mathcal L$, including their coherent naturality. For $X,Y\in\mathcal A$, the cited mapping-space formula computes both source and target mapping spaces by $\underline{\operatorname{Map}}_{\mathcal M}(X,Y)$, and the induced map is the identity. Every object of $\mathcal L$ has such a bifibrant representative. Therefore $J$ is fully faithful on all mapping spaces, with the coherent compositions supplied by the simplicial inclusion.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.3.7.6, localized-presheaf part; HA Theorem 1.3.4.20. Derived identity adjunction as in Cisinski Theorem 7.5.30.

proof.text: For a projectively fibrant presheaf $Z$, step 2 and [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization] identify, for each $f:A\to B$ in $S$, the map $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}^h(A,Z)$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(E(qB),E(qZ))\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P}(E(qA),E(qZ))$. Here $q$ denotes the original coherent localization, not the cofibrant replacement map of step 3. Consequently $Z$ is $S$-local exactly when $E(qZ)$ is $\overline S$-local. Every object of $\mathcal P$ has a projectively fibrant representative by step 2 and the replacement clause of the cited node. If this object is local, so is that representative, since equivalent targets give equivalent mapping spaces. Its projective cofibrant replacement is a trivial fibration to a fibrant object, hence is itself projectively fibrant; it remains local by the same mapping-space invariance. It is therefore bifibrant in $L_S\mathcal M$, by [lem-coef-simplicial-bousfield-model-structure]. Conversely each localized bifibrant object is an $S$-local projectively fibrant presheaf. The essential image of $EJ$ is thus exactly $\mathcal P_{\overline S\text{-loc}}$. With step 5 this gives the required equivalence $\mathcal L\simeq\mathcal P_{\overline S\text{-loc}}$.

source.place: Proof of Proposition A.3.7.6: identify the local full subcategory through derived mapping spaces; essential-image argument written out.

proof.text: Finally [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], applied first to $\mathcal M$ and then to $L_S\mathcal M$, gives the full functor-infinity-category universal properties for $W_{\mathrm{obj}}$ and $W_S$, respectively. Composing either universal localization map with the equivalence constructed in steps 2 or 6 preserves that property: restriction along an equivalence of target infinity categories is an equivalence on their functor infinity categories. In the second case the functor from the ordinary presheaf category is the localized functor followed by the equivalence onto the local full subcategory; the inclusion of that subcategory into $\mathcal P$ is the right adjoint $EJ$, not the localization map. The mapping-space comparisons in steps 5-6 and the evaluation comparison in step 2 retain coherent composition. Hence neither of the assertions is merely an equivalence of ordinary homotopy categories.

source.place: Theorem 1.3.4.20 and Remark 1.3.4.16; invariance of the universal property under the established target equivalences.

The first localization is the actual curried objectwise evaluation. The local target is the full orthogonal subcategory, defined independently of the Bousfield model. Source evaluation on squares to id_Z is the canonical precomposition mapping-space test. The local comparison is normalized on all simplices of the ordinary full subcategory of fibrant local representatives. The ambient universe is max (u+1) v; no nonemptiness or endpoint cofibrancy condition is imposed. Added statement dependencies are already landed interfaces.
